title: Preserve full item token counts before embedding cache and chunk slicing
applies_when: A multimodal scheduler's overlap helper returns a token count larger than the requested chunk, especially for one item with multiple disjoint runs, and a candidate proposes replacing it with the intersection length.
lesson: First identify what the count sizes. An overlap helper may select items while returning each selected item's full encoded length. SGLang _item_overlap uses this contract for both single-run and multi-run items: full counts split concatenated whole-item encoder output and validate full cache entries; _slice_item_chunk clips only after that. A partial chunk of a five-token item still needs a split size of five, not one. Trace encoder output, split sizes, cache identity and the final slice together before changing a suspicious sum. Preserve the original full-item extent across repeated chunks unless the actual encoder is incremental.
avoid_when: A true chunk-local encoder or a cache storing only partial embeddings needs a different count. Full counts do not establish that offsets, embedding order, collision handling or every encoder are correct. The cited source refutes the intersection-count premise; it does not qualify package imports, audio/image encoders, server execution, GPU numerics or performance. Reopen for a supported producer/consumer mismatch with actual output rather than fabricate an expected intersection split.

evidence.note: _item_overlap returns the complete selected item's count; the separate _slice_item_chunk performs chunk clipping. This is a pinned source contract, not a full native integration result.
The batching consumer uses full counts for cache validation and splitting whole encoder output, including the concatenated tensor path.
The per-item consumer caches complete embeddings and slices the requested chunk afterward. No end-to-end correctness or speed claim follows from this source observation.
